warnings:
FEDERATED BEAT CENTRALISED. Check two things, in this order, before concluding anything.
      (1) Leakage. Confirm no identity and no image index is shared between any node and the held-out set. If they are, the run is invalid.
      (2) Matched tuning. Centralised is only an upper bound if it is regularised at least as well as the federated arm. An under-regularised baseline overfits and stops bounding anything, which looks identical to leakage in this table but is not. run_centralised trains one pooled client under the same rounds, epochs and proximal term, so this should hold - but if you have changed either arm's hyperparameters independently, re-check it.
      A small margin after both checks pass is a real, reportable result: averaging across heterogeneous clients is itself a regulariser, and on small non-IID data it can beat pooling.

matched_budget.note: identical to the federated arm in every respect except that one client holds all the data

three_way.eval_sets: gallery 1750 identities | 33250 mate probes | 101114 non-mate probes | 6000 verification pairs

dp_sweep.note: epsilon is update-level and assumes full participation; sigma=0 means clipping only, which carries no formal guarantee and is reported as infinite epsilon

masking.protocol: pairwise Diffie-Hellman key agreement; lower-indexed node adds the mask, higher-indexed subtracts it; masks cancel in the sum
masking.limitation: single-masked, so dropout recovery reveals pairwise masks; a production deployment adds a Shamir-shared self-mask to close that gap

templates.note: templates protect a watchlist at rest and defeat cross-site linkage; they do not defend a live compromised node, which holds the key and sees its own camera feed regardless

identity_level.nonmembers: images of identities never seen by any node
identity_level.caveat: this measures enrolment, not training-set membership; it scores near 1.0 on almost any working model and is NOT comparable with [4]
